chromatic.constantStructure@1.1.summary: Plane into B♭7 with its own shape from above: F6 → C7 → B7 → B♭7.
chromatic.constantStructure@1.1.deepDive: Constant structure keeps one chord shape and moves it in parallel, so the ear follows the shape rather than a key. F6 keeps the downbeat, then B♭7's exact shape slides down by half steps (C → B → B♭). Every voice moves a semitone at a time, the smoothest voice leading there is, while the passing chords come from outside the key.
chromatic.constantStructure@1.1.recreateRule: Near the end of a chord, play the next chord's exact shape a half step (or a whole step) above it and slide the whole hand down into it.

functional.secondaryTwoFive@2.1.summary: Replace B♭7 with the target's own ii–V: Gm9 → C7(♭9) → F6.
functional.secondaryTwoFive@2.1.deepDive: F6 is the I chord. Putting its own ii–V in front briefly makes it sound like home: C is a perfect 5th above F, and G is a 5th above that. The guide tones barely move: B♭ → B♭ → A, F → E → F. You give up the colour of B♭7 and get the strongest pull in tonal harmony instead: the root falls a 5th, twice.
functional.secondaryTwoFive@2.1.recreateRule: Any major or minor chord can get its own ii–V: from the target, go up a 5th for the V and another 5th for the ii.

dominant.tritoneSub@8.3.summary: Swap D7(♭9) for A♭9, the dominant a tritone away.
dominant.tritoneSub@8.3.deepDive:
D7(♭9) and A♭9 share the same tritone: F♯–C (3rd and ♭7 of D7) are G♭–C (♭7 and 3rd of A♭7), the same keys spelled differently. That interval is what makes a dominant want to resolve, so the substitute still lands on Gm7. The difference is the bass, which now slides down a half step (A♭ → G) instead of falling a 5th.

A♭ Lydian dominant uses exactly the same 7 notes as D altered: both are modes of E♭ melodic minor. Soloing over the sub is the same as playing altered over the original.
dominant.tritoneSub@8.3.recreateRule: Any dominant 7 can be replaced by the dominant 7 a tritone (♭5) away. The 3rd and ♭7 swap roles, and the bass moves by a half step.

voicing.upperStructureBVI@8.3.summary: Same chord, new voicing: a B♭ major triad over a D–C–F♯ shell gives D7(♯9,♭13).
voicing.upperStructureBVI@8.3.deepDive: The left hand holds only what defines the dominant: the root, the ♭7 (C) and the 3rd (F♯). The right hand plays a plain B♭ triad (B♭ D F), which over D reads as ♭13, root and ♯9. The shape is easy and the tension is high. B♭ and D and F are already in Gm7, so the resolution is effortless.
voicing.upperStructureBVI@8.3.recreateRule: Over a dominant, play the major triad built on its ♭13 (a major 3rd below the root) above a root–♭7–3 shell. You get a 7(♯9,♭13).

gospel.halfStepTurnaround@10.1.summary: C7 → F6 becomes B♭/C → G♭13(♯11) → F6.
gospel.halfStepTurnaround@10.1.deepDive: B♭/C is a C9sus: a B♭ triad over C. It's the gospel way to sound the dominant while holding back the 3rd. G♭13(♯11) is the tritone sub of C7, voiced as a 13(♯11) cluster a half step above F. Each voice either slides down a half step or stays put as it lands on F6.
gospel.halfStepTurnaround@10.1.recreateRule: Before a tonic, play a 13(♯11) chord a half step above it and slide the whole shape down. Put IV/V in front (a triad on the dominant's ♭7, over its root) for the sus colour.

modal.backdoorTwoFive@10.1.summary: Come in through the back door: B♭m7 → E♭9 → F6, instead of C7 → F6.
modal.backdoorTwoFive@10.1.deepDive: B♭m7 and E♭9 are borrowed from F minor (iv and ♭VII7). E♭9 has no leading tone. Its ♭7 (D♭) falls a half step to C, the 5th of F, its 3rd (G) moves a step into the tonic chord, and the root rises a whole step home. It's a darker, bluesier cadence than C7 → F6, with no tritone resolving.
modal.backdoorTwoFive@10.1.recreateRule: For a major I, approach from iv m7 → ♭VII7: the minor chord a 4th above the tonic, then the dominant a whole step below it.

functional.secondaryTwoFive@11.3.summary: Put the related ii in front of the dominant: Am7♭5 → D7(♭9) → Gm7.
functional.secondaryTwoFive@11.3.deepDive: D7 already resolves down a 5th to Gm7. Every dominant has a "related ii", the minor chord a 5th above its root. Inserting it turns one chord into a full ii–V and doubles the forward motion. The target is minor, so the ii is half-diminished (Am7♭5), borrowed from G harmonic minor. Guide tones: C → C → B♭, G → F♯ → F.
functional.secondaryTwoFive@11.3.recreateRule: Any dominant can borrow its related ii: the minor 7 chord a 5th above its root (m7♭5 if the target is minor).
